llm_summary: The run reached Act 2 with a functional but increasingly attack-heavy deck and no potions remaining. HP steadily declined through Act 2, leaving only 38/80 HP for the final fight. The decisive failure was in the opening turn of that fight: Whirlwind+ was chosen over available Defends, and the next logged state showed HP falling to 20 while both enemies remained alive.

llm_lessons.title: At low HP, prioritize immediate defense over nonlethal damage
llm_lessons.situation: When entering a fight at low HP and the hand contains legal block cards, especially against multiple enemies, use defense unless the attack clearly secures a kill.
llm_lessons.lesson: Do not spend the opening turn on Whirlwind or another broad attack merely for damage when survival is uncertain. In the final fight, choose a Defend line first because the enemies were still substantially alive and two Defends were legal.
evidence_points: Turn 1 began at 38/80 HP with 0 Block; the hand contained two Defends, while Whirlwind+ was selected.
Turn 2 began at 20/80 HP with 0 Block, and Shelled Parasite still had 54/72 HP while Fungi Beast still had 25/25 HP.
The final combat summary records Whirlwind+ followed by Defend, Bash+, and Wild Strike, ending the logged sequence at only 20/80 HP.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The chosen attack did not immediately resolve either enemy, and the next state showed an 18-HP decline with no block remaining. The exact incoming damage is not inferable from the earlier DEBUG intent, but the state transition demonstrates that the aggressive opening failed to create a safe position.

llm_lessons.title: Stop adding redundant attacks when the deck already has damage
llm_lessons.situation: When a reward offers another copy of an attack already represented in the deck, particularly after HP has begun eroding, compare it against skipping and preserving draw quality or defensive density.
llm_lessons.lesson: Prefer skipping redundant attack rewards unless the new copy fills a specific role. This run took a second Wild Strike and a second Pommel Strike, while the final 23-card deck remained attack-heavy; future runs should be more selective and value defensive or scaling cards when available.
evidence_points: At Act 1 Floor 8, Wild Strike was taken even though the final build contains two Wild Strikes.
At Act 2 Floor 21, Pommel Strike was taken even though the final build contains two Pommel Strikes, and skipping was an available alternative.
The final 23-card deck contains four Defends but repeated copies of Pommel Strike, Wild Strike, and Shockwave alongside many other attacks.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The selections increased deck size and repetition without adding a new defensive function. This is not proof that either individual pick caused the loss, but the pattern made it harder to draw a survival-oriented hand in the final combat, where the opening hand had only defensive options that needed to be prioritized carefully.
